subject: Zambia
note: Cited to pinned Wikipedia revisions (trusted_secondary): Quadripoint and Kazungula Bridge. The page itself says the arrangement is not legally settled ('widely believed'). Borders review needed before release: this is shown with Natural Earth lines, which draw the four countries touching.

claims.text: Older sources claimed a quadripoint where Namibia, Botswana, Zambia and Zimbabwe meet at the Chobe-Zambezi confluence.
In 1970, South Africa informed Botswana that there was no common border between Botswana and Zambia, claiming a quadripoint existed.
There was a confrontation and shots were fired at the Kazungula Ferry; some years later the Rhodesian Army attacked and sank the ferry.
It is now widely believed that instead two separate tripoints exist about 100 to 150 metres apart.
The existence of a short boundary of about 150 metres between Zambia and Botswana was agreed by all four states in the 2006-10 period.
The Kazungula Bridge opened for traffic in May 2021; it is curved to avoid the nearby borders of Zimbabwe and Namibia.
